name: Brunswick
takeaway: Brunswick is a NOPEC member — rate jumped from 8.999¢ to 9.999¢ June 1, 2026. Term expires Dec 31, 2026. Renewal cycle starting now.
hook: Brunswick is on NOPEC — hit 9.999 cents in June and that contract runs out at the end of December. Have your accounts there looked at anything before the renewal locks in?
notes: City of Brunswick, Medina County. Ohio Edison (FirstEnergy) territory. NOPEC member community — do NOT confuse with the separate Medina County aggregation program (Dynegy 9.50¢ through 2028). Brunswick is NOPEC, not Medina County program. NOPEC rate 8.999¢ → 9.999¢ June 1 2026 (+11.1%). Term expires Dec 31 2026 — renewal expected but not yet announced. Accounts that opt out of NOPEC are on Ohio Edison standard supply.

name: Medina City
takeaway: Medina City aggregation program (Dynegy) repriced from 6.05¢ to 9.50¢ in May 2026 — a 57% increase. Accounts are locked in through June 2028 but can opt out individually.
hook: Medina City aggregation just jumped 57% — from 6.05 to 9.50 cents — and accounts are locked in through 2028. Most don't know they can opt out. That's the conversation.
notes: Ohio Edison territory. Medina County seat. Medina County aggregation program 9.50¢/kWh through June 2028. Opt-out accounts are on a higher standard offer.

name: Struthers

name: Poland Township
takeaway: Poland Township Dynegy contract expired May 2026 — accounts likely off the program now. Active commercial base near I-680 corridor.
hook: Poland Township's Dynegy aggregation contract just expired last month at 8.69 cents. Are those accounts on a new deal or did they fall off to Ohio Edison standard?

name: Hubbard
takeaway: Hubbard operates its own municipal electric department — exempt from retail electric choice. No competitive supply possible. Blacklisted.
notes: City of Hubbard Electric — municipal utility. Not eligible for competitive electric supply. Has natural gas aggregation (Major Energy) but electric is municipal-only.

name: Licking County / Pataskala
takeaway: Pataskala and Licking County eastern Columbus suburbs on AEP Ohio — rate moving from 9.08¢ to 10.01¢ in June 2026. Fast-growing exurb with commercial development.
hook: Pataskala and the eastern Licking County corridor — AEP territory going up to 10¢ in June. Lot of new commercial build-out that hasn't set up supply contracts.
notes: AEP Ohio territory. Licking County. Fast-growing Columbus exurb east of Columbus. Commercial development along Route 40 and I-70. Aggregation rate exposure June 2026.

name: Athens County (Rural AEP)
takeaway: Rural Athens County is split between AEP Ohio and electric cooperative (South Central Power, Buckeye Rural Electric) territory. Verify utility by address before calling.
hook: Athens County rural addresses — do you know if you're on AEP Ohio or a rural electric co-op? The whole county is a mix, so it depends on the address.
notes: Rural Athens County is shared between AEP Ohio and electric cooperatives (South Central Power Co., Buckeye Rural Electric). AEP Ohio addresses are eligible for competitive supply; co-op addresses are exempt. Verify by service address.

name: Guernsey / Noble / Morgan Counties
takeaway: Rural SE Ohio tri-county area (Guernsey/Noble/Morgan) is shared between AEP Ohio and Guernsey-Muskingum Electric Co-op. Verify utility by address — co-op territory is exempt from retail choice.
hook: Guernsey/Noble/Morgan County rural accounts — do you know if you're on AEP Ohio or the Guernsey-Muskingum co-op? The territories are mixed out there.
notes: AEP Ohio and Guernsey-Muskingum Electric Cooperative shared territory. AEP accounts eligible for competitive supply; GMEC co-op accounts exempt. Verify utility on bill before calling.

name: Russells Point
takeaway: Dynegy Logan County program covers Russells Point only, 9.26¢/kWh from Dec 2025 through Dec 2026.
notes: Lakeview village has its own municipal electric utility and is not in this program.
